sun.upright:
Aries is the sign that starts things, and the Ten of Swords is about as finished as a card gets, so on an Aries Sun it lands on the part of you that hates an ending most. The Sun is exalted in Aries, which means it's at its proudest and most idealised in your sign. You're used to your will being the strongest thing in the room. This card says something you put that will behind has come to a full stop, a plan, a role, a version of yourself you were very publicly building, and trying harder isn't going to rescue it.

What you'll notice first is the itch to get up. The man in the picture is flat on the ground, and an Aries Sun wants him on his feet by the next frame, swords and all. There's help in the astrology, to be fair. Gemini sits two signs from Aries, a sextile, and air feeds fire, so once you've actually let the thing end, the next idea catches very fast. The trouble is the order you do it in. I've seen plenty of Aries Suns start the next project the same week the last one collapsed, and then wonder why it feels hollow. Pride takes a knock with this card, and it's worth letting it sting for a while before you build over the top of it.

At work it might be the venture you launched with a lot of noise, now wound up, or the promotion that went to somebody else. In sport it can be the season you've had to sit out. With a rival it's admitting they won this one. Give yourself a proper gap before the next start, a fortnight at least, and don't announce anything during it.
sun.reversed:
Upside down, this card often catches an Aries Sun getting up too fast. You've decided the collapse didn't count. The business failed or the relationship ended, and within days you were telling everyone about the next plan, which is mostly the old plan with a new name. The Sun rules the middle ten degrees of Aries, the Three of Wands, a card about sending your ventures out into the world, and reversed this can feel like standing on the shore with nothing going out.

At work it shows as picking a fight with whoever made the call, long after it was made. In the body it's training through something that needed rest. With friends it's refusing to talk about what happened, because talking about it feels like losing twice. Tell one person the full story of what went wrong, start to finish, before you begin anything new.

moon.upright:
You don't usually stay down long. An Aries Moon feels things fast and hot, gets angry, says so, and is often over it by dinner, which people who don't know you mistake for not caring. What you need is to do something with a feeling. This card shows a feeling with nothing left to do. Something hurt you, or ended, or you found out a thing you can't unknow, and the usual burst of temper has burned out and left you lying flat in it.

Gemini and Aries are two signs apart, a sextile, and air feeds fire, which sounds friendly and mostly is. Here it has a catch. Gemini is the storytelling mind, and the card puts the Sun on it, so every thought gets lit up and handed to your temper as fuel. You lie awake building the case. The ex, the friend who let you down, the boss who said that thing in front of everyone, each gets a longer and worse version every time you run it. The anger keeps catching because the mind keeps feeding it, and for a Moon whose feelings are meant to burn off quickly, that's exhausting.

The body shows it first, usually as broken sleep and a short fuse in the morning. With a partner it's snapping about the dishes when it's really about something from weeks ago. With a parent it can be an old grievance that flared up and hasn't settled. Most Aries Moons I've known find the edge only comes off with movement, a long walk uphill, a hard swim, something that leaves you too tired to rehearse the argument.
moon.reversed:
This card reversed on an Aries Moon is often anger that's got nowhere to go and has turned round on you. The blow landed a while ago. You didn't cry and you didn't shout, you just got busy, and the feeling that should have burned out in a day has been smouldering for weeks. Mars rules Aries, and a Mars-ruled Moon under a reversed Ten can pick small fights to avoid the big one.

In the body it's tension you can't shake, the clenched jaw, restless legs at night. At home it's slamming cupboards over nothing. At work it's the short email you regret by lunchtime. Somewhere in there is sadness an Aries Moon would rather not own up to, because sad feels weaker than angry. Let yourself be sad about it for one evening, properly, without doing anything useful.

rising.upright:
Aries rising walks in as if it's already decided to win, chin up, first to speak, a bit quick with the handshake. Drawn as your mask, this card says that front has taken a knock and people can see it. Maybe you've just lost something public, a job, a relationship everybody knew about, a contest you were meant to take, and you're turning up to things as the person it happened to.

The odd comfort in the astrology is that the card's planet is exalted in your rising sign. The Sun is honoured in Aries, so even flat on the ground there's some shine on you. People who meet you in this state tend to read courage in it, the fact that you came at all. From the inside it doesn't feel like courage. It feels like walking into a room where everyone knows, and Mars, your chart ruler, wants to get the first word in so nobody gets the chance to pity you. The sextile from Gemini, air feeding the fire, makes the quick joke and the brisk explanation come easily. Too easily, sometimes. People can tell when you've rehearsed it.

At a new job it's starting on the bottom rung after being higher up somewhere else. At a family gathering it's the first time you've been seen since the news got round. With someone you've just started dating it's deciding how soon to tell them. Try saying it once, in one plain sentence, the first time it comes up, and then change the subject yourself.
rising.reversed:
Aries rising with this card reversed tends to meet everyone braced for the next hit. You got knocked down a while back, and you're up, and you're fine, and you walk into every room ready for a fight that isn't coming. Strangers read it as prickly. The quick temper that usually passes for honesty starts to look defensive.

In interviews it turns up as over-explaining the gap on your CV. In a new friendship it's testing people early to see if they'll let you down. At the gym or on the field it can be pushing hard to prove you're back, which is how Aries rising ends up hurt twice. Walk into the next new place with your shoulders down on purpose, and wait to be asked before you tell anyone your story.

sun.upright:
The house, the savings, the twelve-year friendship, the job you got good at by staying in it. A Taurus Sun builds slowly and means it to last, so an ending as flat and total as this one lands hard on you, harder than on most signs, because you weren't planning on this thing ever needing to end. Gemini is the sign right next door to Taurus, a semi-sextile, and neighbours like that have little in common. Gemini can move on in an afternoon. You can't, and you're not built to.

The element friction is worth naming. Earth wants proof and air deals in ideas, and every sword in this suit is an idea. A Taurus Sun can hear that something is finished, can even say so out loud, and still not believe it until the evidence is sitting on the table. So you go on paying for the gym membership, keeping the spare room made up, turning up to a job that's already been restructured out from under you. In your sign the card's Sun has no dignity of its own and takes its colour from Venus, which is about value, what things are worth to you. What's hard here is admitting that something you valued has gone, whatever it's still costing you.

With money it might be an investment or a business that won't come back, and what really hurts is the plan you had for it. With a partner it's a relationship you've been keeping the furniture of. Pick the one thing you're still paying for, in cash or in time, for something that's over, and cancel it.
sun.reversed:
For a Taurus Sun the reversed card often looks like having made yourself comfortable at the bottom. The worst came and went some time ago, and instead of getting up you've furnished the place. It's familiar, you know where everything is, and a fixed earth sign can mistake that for being settled. Starting again, to the Venus side of you, feels like giving up what you'd earned.

At work it's staying on in a role that's shrunk around you, because leaving would mean admitting what happened. With money it's the loss you won't write off. In the body it can be a heaviness, sleeping long and waking tired. You don't need a big leap. Taurus recovers one physical step at a time, so pick a small practical thing that belongs to the next chapter and do it before the week's out.

moon.upright:
Every sword in this suit is a thought, and ten is where the thinking has run out of places to go. That's hard on a Taurus Moon, because comfort for you is physical. A full fridge, a warm bed, the same walk at the same time, a hand you know. Earth and air are opposite kinds of element, talk against proof, so what you might be living with is a head full of the worst possible story and a body that has simply stopped.

That's how a Taurus Moon hits bottom. Quietly. You don't make a scene, you go heavy. You sleep more, eat what's easy, cancel what you can, and sit in the same chair longer than you meant to. The Sun is just a visitor in Taurus, coloured by Venus, so what the card lights up here is comfort itself, what you've been leaning on to feel all right and whether it still works. Gemini sits right beside Taurus in the zodiac, a semi-sextile, and each has what the other lacks. What Gemini has that you don't is the knack of dropping a thing once it's done. You hold on, and your body holds on with you.

With a partner it's being hard to reach, polite and far away. With food and sleep it's the rhythm sliding, late nights and skipped meals, or the reverse. Around money it can be spending to feel better, small things, often. Cook one proper meal, eat it slowly at a table, and see what you feel once you've finished.
moon.reversed:
When the Ten is upside down, a Taurus Moon tends to hold the ending in the body long after the mind has moved on. You've said you're over it and mostly you mean it, but your shoulders haven't heard, and your appetite hasn't either. Fixed earth keeps things. Usually that's your strength. Reversed, it means keeping the ache as well.

Sleep is the place to watch, heavy and unrefreshing, or waking at four with the old story going. At home it can be keeping everything exactly as it was, the photos, the chair, the Saturday routine built for two. With friends it's saying yes to plans and quietly dreading them. Change one physical thing in the house that belonged to the old arrangement, move it, give it away, paint over it, and notice how the room feels afterwards.

rising.upright:
People tend to find Taurus rising reassuring. You come across as calm, unhurried, good to be around, somebody who won't make a fuss. Venus rules your Ascendant, so there's usually some ease and grace in how you arrive. With this card showing on your mask, what's under that calm is a story that's just finished, badly. You're turning up to things steady on the outside while something has come to a full stop behind it.

Air and earth pull against each other, the idea against the proof, and on your Ascendant that shows up as a gap between how you look and what's going on. Strangers read the earth. They see the steady handshake and the unbothered face, and they have no idea. Some of that is a gift, because it gets you through the week. Some of it isn't, because nobody offers help to someone who looks fine. Gemini is the next sign along from Taurus, and neighbours like that don't speak the same language, so the mind's version of events and the body's version stay oddly separate. You can talk about what happened in a perfectly even voice and then find you can't face the supermarket.

At work it's being the unflappable one during a restructure you're privately gutted by. In a new relationship it's being lovely company and giving away nothing of what you've just come out of. Around family it's being the one everybody leans on while you're barely upright. Hardly anyone will guess, which is what you were going for, and it's lonely.
rising.reversed:
Taurus rising with the card reversed can look closed for business. You've been through something, you're recovering, and the way a fixed earth Ascendant recovers is by not moving much. People read that as stubborn or cold. What it actually is, most of the time, is caution. You've decided nothing new is getting in until you're sure.

In a new job this is the colleague who takes months to warm up. With friends it's turning down the invitation before you've heard what it is. On dating apps it's the profile you never finish. The pace is yours to set and nobody should hurry you, though a total stop can go on for years if you let it. Say yes to one low-stakes thing you'd normally refuse, a coffee, a class, a walk with someone new.

sun.upright:
This card is one of Gemini's own. It's the Sun in the last ten degrees of your sign, so if your birthday falls in the final stretch of Gemini it's the card of your own decan, and even if it doesn't, it's family. It's also the one Gemini card that doesn't leave a door open. A Gemini Sun is built on options, the second plan, the other conversation, the chance to change your mind on Thursday. What this card shows is what happens when you run out.

Air on air, the same element, amplifies things, and the Sun has no special dignity here and takes on Mercury's colouring, so it lights up the thinking. You'll recognise the feeling. A story you've been telling yourself about who you are and where this is all going has been followed right to the last page. Maybe it's the career idea you've talked about for years. Maybe it's the version of yourself as the one who always has something new on the go. Either way you've thought it through and there's nothing left on the page. For a sign that hates being cornered, that's hard. There's an odd relief in it too, and I've seen Gemini Suns go very quiet with it.

At work it might mean finally dropping the side project you've half-done for years. With a sibling, and Gemini often has one who matters, it can be an old family role you've stopped being willing to play. Write the story you've just finished telling yourself as a single paragraph, then put it away and don't edit it.
sun.reversed:
When a Gemini Sun gets this card reversed, the story that should have ended keeps getting retold. You've explained what happened to nine people, each with a slightly different angle, and every version keeps it alive a little longer. Upside down, the doubled air means the talking has replaced the grieving. You're across every detail and you haven't felt much of it.

At work it shows up as starting three new things so you don't have to admit the last one failed. Socially it's the group chat where you've become the one with the ongoing drama. At night it's the replay at two in the morning, with better lines than you actually said. Pick one person, tell them the whole thing properly one more time, and then agree with yourself that's the last telling for a while.

moon.upright:
You read the article, you ask the second question, you check the message again to see what they really meant. A Gemini Moon calms itself down by knowing, and once you understand a thing you can usually stop worrying about it. This card is that habit at the very end of its rope. You've found out everything there was to find out. The whole picture is in front of you, lit up, and it didn't make you feel any better.

The card sits in the last ten degrees of Gemini, so it's your Moon sign's own card, and air meeting air turns the volume up. For a Gemini Moon that happens in the nerves. You're tired in a buzzing, wired way. Your mind's been going at full speed on one thing, a break-up, a friend's crisis, news you weren't expecting, and it's worked through every possibility and landed on the worst. There's a stillness at the bottom of that, when the thinking finally runs out of road, and a Gemini Moon can be quite frightened of it because it's so unfamiliar.

With your phone this is the scrolling that won't stop. With friends it's talking about it to everyone and still feeling on your own. With sleep it's lying awake narrating. When did you last go a whole evening without any input at all, no screen, no podcast, nobody to text?
moon.reversed:
Reversed, this card on a Gemini Moon usually means the replay button's stuck. The worst has passed, you know it has, and the mind keeps rewinding to the moment it happened as if a different ending might turn up. Mercury colours the Sun in Gemini, and upside down that turns into restlessness with nothing to chew on except the past.

It shows up as rereading old messages, checking an ex's profile, going over one conversation with a friend for the fourth time. You may feel jittery, with your stomach unsettled by it. With the people closest to you it can sound like cheerfulness while you're actually spinning. Give your mind something new and absorbing that has nothing to do with any of it, a course, a language, a long novel, and let the old tape run down on its own.

rising.upright:
Gemini rising usually gets through a first meeting on talk. You ask the questions, you find the joke, and ten minutes in the other person has told you where they grew up. Mercury rules your Ascendant, so words are how you open every door. Drawn for your mask, and coming from your own rising sign, this card says the words have run a bit dry. People are meeting a quieter version of you, somebody who's clearly just finished something big.

Same element, air on air, so the card doesn't sit awkwardly on you. You can even make it funny. That's the Gemini rising talent and also the trap. You're so good at telling the story of what happened, the lost job, the break-up, the move that fell through, with perfect timing and a self-deprecating punchline, that people laugh and never realise how flat you are underneath. Some part of you probably wants that, since it's a way to be seen without really being seen. But the card has the Sun in it, and the Sun doesn't do cover well. Something of the tiredness gets through in the pauses.

In meetings it's being slower than usual and having people notice. In a new friendship it's the first time you don't fill the silence. With neighbours or at the school gate it's the anecdote you've told so often it's worn smooth. The next time someone asks how you are, give an answer that isn't a story.
rising.reversed:
With the card reversed, Gemini rising can come across as jumpy. You're chatting fast, changing subjects, laughing a beat too early, and people who don't know you pick up a nervy edge without knowing what it's about. What it's usually about is a recent ending you haven't let finish. Every new conversation is a chance to not think about it, so you have a lot of them.

At a party it's being everywhere and remembering nobody. At work it's saying yes to every meeting. With someone new it's texting a lot and saying very little. Most people won't mind, and some will enjoy it. The tiredness catches up with you, though, usually on a Sunday. Keep one evening completely free of company and see what you think about when there's nobody to talk to.

sun.upright:
Somebody has to hold a family together, and with a Cancer Sun it's usually you. Your sense of who you are is built around looking after something, a household, a team at work, a friend who's always in trouble. This card says one of those roles has ended. Maybe a child has left home, or the parent you were caring for doesn't need you the same way, or the group you held together for years has quietly broken up. What's gone is partly the people and partly the version of you that was built around them.

In Cancer the Sun has no special standing and takes on the Moon's colouring, since the Moon rules your sign, so the card's light here turns toward memory and home. You'll find yourself going back over things, the old house, the years when everyone still came round for Sunday lunch. Air and water are neutral with each other, and they have to be introduced. The card's air wants to think the ending through to its last line and file it. Cancer's water wants to feel it for as long as it takes. So you might have the odd experience of knowing perfectly well that it's over and still setting a place at the table. It takes a while for the two to catch up with each other.

At home it might be the empty room you keep walking past. At work, if you've been the one who mothers the team, it could be a restructure that's scattered them. With your own mother, or whoever played that part, it can be a shift in who looks after whom. Choose one thing from the old arrangement to keep, deliberately, and let the rest go.
sun.reversed:
A Cancer Sun with this card reversed usually hasn't let go, and knows it. The ending came, and you've kept on caring for the thing that ended. You still ring the ex's mother. You're still doing the books for a club that folded. You keep the family group chat going on your own. The crab doesn't let go of what it's gripping, and most of the time that's what makes you so good to have around.

Around the home it can look like a museum of the old life. At work it's taking on responsibility for people who've moved on. With your own energy it's running on empty while you look after everyone else. Pick one thing you're still holding for somebody, hand it back or put it down, and tell them kindly that you have.

moon.upright:
You noticed the change in their voice on the phone before anyone else did. A Cancer Moon is always half-listening for trouble, the silence at dinner, the bill left unopened on the bench, and you start worrying well before anyone else knows there's anything to worry about. It's how you keep your people safe. What this card describes is the thing you were worrying about actually happening. And many Cancer Moons will recognise the strange calm that follows, because all that bracing finally has somewhere to land.

Gemini is the sign just before Cancer, a semi-sextile, neighbours with very little in common. Gemini can look at a disaster and describe it. You feel it in your chest and your stomach and don't have words for it for a while. The card's element and yours are neutral to each other, air and water, and neither one knows how the other works. So there may be a gap between what you understand about what happened and what you feel, and it can be days before the two meet. The Sun takes on the Moon's colouring in your sign, which brings memory into it. Old losses tend to come back with the new one, a grandparent, the first house, a friend you lost touch with at school, as if they'd been waiting.

At home you'll want to shut the door and stay in. With family it might be the one person you can cry in front of. In the body it's often the appetite, gone or looking for comfort, and sleep that comes in short pieces. Let someone bring you a meal, and don't insist on washing up.
moon.reversed:
Upside down, the Ten can leave a Cancer Moon bracing for something that's already been and gone. The crisis is over. The family's more or less settled, the money's sorted, the relationship has ended cleanly enough. And you're still waiting for the phone to ring with bad news, still sleeping lightly, still checking. A Moon in its own sign holds on to everything, and that includes fear.

At home it can look like fussing over the people who got through it, a partner or a grown child who's actually fine. In the body it's a knot that won't loosen. With old friends it's retelling the worst part as if it happened yesterday. Say to yourself, out loud if it helps, what's actually true about how things stand, one fact at a time, and let your breathing slow while you do it.

rising.upright:
Cancer rising meets the world carefully. You're kind and attentive with new people but you keep a bit of shell up, and you tend to look after others in a room before you let anyone look after you. The Moon rules your Ascendant, which is why strangers can often read your mood on your face before you've said a word. Drawn in this position, the card says what they're reading is that you've been through something, and recently.

The Sun is a guest in Cancer, coloured by the Moon, your chart ruler, so it doesn't overpower you. It just shows what's there, and that's the hard part. Cancer rising would usually go into its shell before letting anyone see it at a low point, and this card doesn't give you much of a shell to go into. Gemini, the card's sign, sits right behind Cancer, and the two have little in common. Gemini would chat its way through. You'd retreat. The card sort of forces you out into the open, looking tired, carrying the thing everybody can see you're carrying. People are often kinder about it than you expect.

At a new workplace it's being the quiet one who clearly has a lot going on at home. With other parents it's the conversation you'd rather avoid at pick-up. Meeting a new partner, it's showing up before you feel ready to be seen. When somebody offers help, even a stranger holding a door, let them, and say thank you without explaining yourself.
rising.reversed:
When the card is reversed, Cancer rising tends to go straight back into the shell and stay there. The ending's over and you've recovered, more or less, but the front you've put up since is tighter than before. New people get your politeness, your good manners and your cooking, and not much else. It's safe. It's also lonely, and somewhere you know that.

At work this can be looking after everyone so thoroughly that nobody thinks to look after you. At a party it's spending the evening in the kitchen. With someone new it's disappearing for a week whenever things start to feel close. Pick one person you'd like to know better and let them see you on an ordinary bad day, unfixed.

sun.upright:
You're used to being lit from the front. A Leo Sun wants its work seen and its warmth felt, and when things are going well you're the person a room arranges itself around, whether you meant it to or not. This card shows the opposite, somebody face down on the ground, and for a sign with as much pride as yours that's a hard picture to be handed. The Sun rules Leo. It's at home in your sign, strong and easy there, and it's also this card's planet, so the card speaks with your own ruler's voice. You can't really wave it off.

What the Sun does in this card is show everything. Nothing about the ending is hidden, and for a Leo Sun the worst part is often exactly that, the fact that people saw. The show that closed early. The business that folded with everyone watching. Being passed over in front of the whole team. I've seen Leo Suns cope with loss better than almost anyone and then struggle for months with the embarrassment. Leo is fixed fire, though, and fixed fire is slow to go out. Gemini sits in a sextile to Leo, and air keeps fire going, so the same mind that ran the worst-case story can start feeding the next idea, once you let it.

At work it might be a role you were proud of, gone. In love it can be a relationship ending in a way all your friends know about. With a creative project it's the thing you made that nobody came to. Let a couple of people who love you see you properly flattened, without the brave face, and let them be kind to you.
sun.reversed:
Leo with the Ten reversed can overplay the comeback. You've been knocked flat, and instead of resting you're already back on stage, bigger and louder, making sure everyone sees you're fine. The Sun rules your sign and doesn't like being dimmed. Upside down, that can turn into a performance of recovery that wears you out worse than the fall did.

The other version is the fall that becomes the whole show. You tell the story of how badly you were treated at every dinner, and it gets a bit grander each time. At work it can be the dramatic resignation letter you haven't sent and keep redrafting. With a partner it's needing reassurance you won't ask for directly. Tell one person, privately, how much it actually hurt, and skip the performance entirely.

moon.upright:
Nobody came to the birthday, or not the people who mattered. The friend you'd have done anything for took the other side. Your partner forgot, and then forgot that they'd forgotten. A Leo Moon needs to feel it matters to someone, and this card can land on that need like several small betrayals arriving at once. When you get warmth back you're generous to a fault. When you don't, it goes very deep, very fast.

The Sun is at home in Leo. It rules your Moon sign, and it's the card's planet too, so this doesn't feel minor. It feels total. Leo's fixed fire holds a feeling steady for a long time, which is why you're so loyal and also why a hurt takes so long to cool. Gemini is two signs away in a sextile, and on the Moon the air it brings usually means your mind supplies the fuel. You go over who said what, you build the case, and every time you tell it the insult gets hotter. From the inside it's a mix of heartbreak and hurt pride, and a Leo Moon doesn't always like admitting which is which.

With a partner it's the sulk that's really a plea to be chosen. With friends it's pulling back your warmth to see if anyone notices. In the body it tends to show as heaviness and bad sleep, and very little interest in fun. Ask one person directly for the thing you've been hoping they'd offer.
moon.reversed:
The reversed Ten can make a Leo Moon act fine far too convincingly. You were hurt, badly, and the fixed fire in you decided nobody was going to see it, so the smile went on and stayed on. It's impressive. It also means the hurt has nowhere to go but inward, and it comes out sideways, a sharp remark at a friend's dinner, a sudden coolness toward someone who's done nothing wrong.

At home it looks like needing a lot of attention without saying so, and taking it badly when none arrives. With friends it's the grudge kept warm for months. Your appetite for fun drops off, which is always worth noticing with a Leo Moon. Do one thing purely for the pleasure of it, on your own, where nobody's watching, and see whether it lifts anything.

rising.upright:
Leo rising has the Sun as its chart ruler, and this is a Sun card, so whatever it says goes straight to how you come across. Usually that's with some glow. You walk in and people look up. You're warm, a bit theatrical, good at making strangers feel welcome. Drawn for your mask, the Ten of Swords turns the stage lights down. People meeting you are meeting someone who's obviously been through something, and a Leo Ascendant finds being seen like that very hard.

Look at the sky in the picture, black apart from a thin gold line low on the horizon. Leo rising's instinct in a patch like this is to supply the missing light yourself, by being extra bright and extra funny, and when you're this tired it tends to look exactly like what it is. The Sun is at home in Leo, strong and unforced, and the unforced part is what matters here. Gemini's air feeds your fire through the sextile, so honest conversation will bring colour back to your face faster than a performance can.

At work it's walking into the first meeting after a public failure. In a new relationship it's letting someone meet you at a low point, which you'd normally never allow. With your kids, or any young person who looks up to you, it's showing them how a person gets through a bad patch. Go to one thing you'd normally sparkle at and let yourself be ordinary there.
rising.reversed:
With this card upside down, Leo rising may have stopped going out. The fall happened, you've mostly recovered, and the idea of walking in somewhere and being looked at is suddenly too much, so you've stayed home, missed the launch, sent apologies to the wedding. For a sign whose Ascendant is ruled by the Sun, hiding is a very unnatural state and you'll feel dim with it.

The other form is the opposite, a comeback so loud it's a bit brittle, and people pick up on the strain. At work either version costs you, because colleagues can't quite place you. With friends it's being the life of the party one week and unreachable the next. Accept one invitation to something small, dinner with two or three people you like, and go as you are.

sun.upright:
You tried it three different ways and it still came down. Virgo Suns are here to make things work properly. You notice what's broken, you work out how to fix it, and you get a lot of your sense of yourself from being the one who does. The Ten of Swords is something that couldn't be fixed, and for a Virgo Sun that can be harder than the loss itself, because it seems to say something about you.

Gemini squares Virgo. Both are mutable, both are ruled by Mercury, and they sit three signs apart, which is friction that forces something to move. Gemini's Mercury talks and imagines. Yours checks and sorts. The swords are Gemini's, thinking run right to the end of the line, and a Virgo Sun under this card can analyse an ending until you have a complete list of everything you did wrong, in order. Air and earth disagree about what counts as real, so it's worth asking how much of that list is worry and how much is evidence. The Sun does have a foothold in your sign. It rules the first ten degrees of Virgo, the Eight of Pentacles, the card of patient work at the bench, and most Virgo Suns I've known get back on their feet through work like that, something practical and done well, a shelf, a garden bed, a spreadsheet that finally balances.

On the job it's the project you poured care into that got cancelled regardless. With your health routine it can be the regime you followed perfectly that didn't give you what it promised. In a relationship it's the one you kept trying to improve. Put the list of what went wrong in a drawer, and start something with your hands that you can finish in a day.
sun.reversed:
With this card reversed, a Virgo Sun is often still trying to fix something that's finished. The business closed, the relationship ended, the job's gone, and you're still going over the paperwork, reorganising the files, wondering if there's a version that works with a few changes. Your Mercury and Gemini's are square to each other, and upside down the friction gets stuck in the checking.

At work it's the post-mortem that never ends. At home it's cleaning with a slightly desperate edge. In the body it's a tight, wired kind of tiredness. With a partner or a friend it's being critical of them when you're really furious with yourself. Write down three things about the ending that were outside your control, and read them back every time you start the audit again.

moon.upright:
The kitchen's clean, the list is ticked, the week's planned, and everybody you look after has what they need. That's when a Virgo Moon can breathe. When things go wrong you calm yourself by being useful. What this card describes is the point where being useful stops working. Something happened, a redundancy, a break-up, a friend's crisis, that no amount of sorting could have prevented, and the mind has gone through every version of it and arrived at the worst.

Mercury rules Virgo and colours the Sun here, and the card's own sign, Gemini, is Mercury's other home. The two signs are square, though, and at that angle the two Mercuries grind. Gemini's thinking spins and imagines. Your Moon wants it to settle into something practical, and it won't. The elements are at odds as well, air against earth, the worry against the actual facts on the ground. What a Virgo Moon feels at the bottom of this card is usually exhaustion from over-preparing. You braced for every possible outcome and you're too tired to feel much about the one that arrived.

In the body it shows as a knotted stomach and shallow sleep, and as the urge to clean the whole house at eleven at night. At work you might throw yourself into detail so you don't have to feel anything. With a partner you may be sharper than you mean to be. Let one small thing stay undone and messy for a day, the dishes, the inbox, the drawer, and notice that nothing collapses.
moon.reversed:
Reversed, a Virgo Moon tends to protect itself against another collapse by controlling everything within reach. The worst is over. But the lists have got longer, the routines stricter, and you've started checking things you checked an hour ago. Gemini's air squaring your earth does this. The mind hands the body a worry, and the body tries to solve it by keeping order.

It shows up in the home as rules nobody else agreed to, and a partner who's started to feel watched. With food and sleep it can be a regime that's gone a bit joyless. With the people close to you it's the running commentary on how they could do things better. Pick one routine you've tightened since the bad patch, loosen it deliberately for a fortnight, and see who in the house notices first.

rising.upright:
Virgo rising tends to arrive quietly and competently. You're the tidy one, observant, helpful, the person who notices the name tag's spelled wrong and fixes it without fuss. Strangers read you as capable and a bit reserved, and they're usually right. In the mask position this card says something has gone wrong that competence couldn't prevent, and it's visible. People can tell you're depleted even when you've ironed the shirt.

Mercury rules your Ascendant and also rules Gemini, the card's sign, but the two sit square, and the friction shows up in how you present. Part of you wants to explain what happened clearly and accurately, with dates. Part of you wants nobody to know at all. Idea and matter are at odds in this pairing, and for Virgo rising that can mean a neat exterior over a head that's been running worst-case scenarios for weeks. The Sun does rule the first ten degrees of Virgo, the Eight of Pentacles decan, the apprentice's card. If you've had to start again somewhere, a new job, a new town, a level below where you were, that's the flavour of it. Lower down, learning again, doing careful work where nobody knows your history.

In a job interview it's accounting for the gap, calmly. At a new gym or class it's being a beginner in front of strangers. With a new neighbour it's the small talk you have to manage while exhausted. Let one small part of how you look or how you work be imperfect in public, and leave it that way.
rising.reversed:
Virgo rising with the card reversed can come across as a bit too careful. Every sentence is qualified, every email checked twice, every apology in place before anyone's complained. It comes from the fall, the one you've mostly recovered from, and part of you is trying to make sure nothing like it can happen again by getting every small thing right.

People read it as nerves, or sometimes as coldness. At work it's the colleague who over-prepares for a five-minute meeting. In a new relationship it's being so considerate that the other person can't find a way in. With friends it's never letting them help. Next time you make a small mistake in front of someone, let it go without apologising and carry on with the conversation.

sun.upright:
The first thing a Libra Sun will notice about this card is that it isn't fair. Ten swords where one would have done. It's out of proportion, and proportion is what your sign is built on. You want things weighed up, both sides heard, a settlement everyone can live with. This is an ending that came down all on one side, and there's no appeal.

Gemini and Libra are trine, both air, so the card doesn't clash with you, and it turns up whatever's already there. The problem is the Sun itself. The Sun is in fall in Libra, which means it's uncomfortable in your sign and tends to get its way indirectly. A Libra Sun's sense of self often runs through other people, through being liked, being the reasonable one, being one of a couple. So when this card lands on your Sun, whatever ended has often taken some of your identity with it. You were half of something, and you're working out what you are on your own. The doubled air means you can think about it endlessly, rehearsing the conversation where you finally make them see how unfair it was.

With a partner or an ex it's the break-up where they got their story in first. At work it might be a partnership or a deal that collapsed without you having a say. In a friendship group it's the split where people chose sides. Decide what you think happened, keep that version for yourself, and stop trying to get the other person to agree with it.
sun.reversed:
For a Libra Sun the reversed card is often an ending you're still negotiating with. It's over, and you keep going back to agree the terms, to make sure the other person's all right, to have one more reasonable conversation. The Sun is weak in your sign and finds it hard to put its own will first, and upside down that becomes a very drawn-out goodbye.

At work it's the partnership that's formally ended where you're still covering their share. Socially it's staying friendly with an ex because it seems the civilised thing, while it keeps you raw. At home it's avoiding a decision about the flat, the furniture, the dog. Make one decision about what's left without asking anyone's opinion first, and tell them afterwards.

moon.upright:
An atmosphere is the thing you can't stand. A Libra Moon can live with a lot, but a room where two people aren't speaking gets under your skin, so you smooth, you soften, you let small things go to keep the peace, and most of the time it works. This card is where it stopped working. Something came to an end in spite of all the smoothing, a relationship, a friendship, a family arrangement that had been held together mostly by your good manners.

Gemini trines Libra, air to air, so the card moves through you easily. It amplifies, though, and what it amplifies for a Libra Moon is going over it. Was it your fault? Could you have said it better? Would it have lasted if you'd been more patient? The card's planet sits in its fall in Libra, uncomfortable, unable to make itself heard directly, and on your Moon that often shows as feelings you haven't let yourself have because they seemed unfair on the other person. You're sad, and you're angry, and the anger feels impolite, so it stays in your head and turns into analysis.

At home it's the quiet after someone's left, and the odd guilty relief in it. With friends it's taking everyone's side except your own. In the body it's the tired, wired feeling of having been reasonable for too long. Say to one person who won't pass it on exactly what you're angry about, and don't be fair while you do it.
moon.reversed:
This card upside down can leave a Libra Moon unable to be on its own. The ending's done, you're recovering, and you've filled every evening with company so you don't have to hear what the quiet sounds like. Or you've gone back, to the person or to a version of them, because a bad peace felt easier to live with than none at all.

It shows at home as never quite settling into a place you live in alone. With a new partner it's moving too fast because you're rushing to feel paired again. With friends it's agreeing with everyone and saying very little that's yours. The Sun sits badly in Libra, and reversed it goes quiet altogether. Spend one full evening alone on purpose and do exactly what you like, from the food to the music.

rising.upright:
Libra rising gets through almost anything with good manners. People meet you and find you easy, pleasant, well put together, and interested in them. Venus rules your Ascendant, so you've usually got the right thing to say and you look like you've made an effort. Drawn as your mask, this card turns up when something has ended that your manners couldn't save, and you have to keep meeting people while it's still raw.

The card's planet is in fall in your rising sign. The Sun is uncomfortable in Libra, it doesn't get heard, and it has to find a roundabout way to do its job. For your first impression that means the card's full exposure doesn't come across straight. People see graciousness. They see you being lovely about the ex, generous about the job that went to someone else, calm at the party where everyone knows. The trine to Gemini lets you talk about it smoothly, air to air, and the smoothness gets amplified too. Some of it is real grace, some is a very good finish on something that's badly broken, and it's tiring keeping both going.

At work it's congratulating the person who got your role and meaning about half of it. At a wedding it's being seated near someone you'd rather not see. On a first date it's being so agreeable they don't learn a single thing about you. Would anyone who's met you lately have any idea what you've just been through?
rising.reversed:
Libra rising with this card reversed can go a bit brittle. The charm's still on, but people can feel the effort in it. You're smiling a fraction too long, agreeing too fast, and every so often something sharp slips out, a joke with an edge, a remark about an ex that's funnier than it is kind. It's a sign the recovery is going on underneath and hasn't reached the surface yet.

At work you might be keeping a peace that's no longer your job to keep. With new people it's saying everything's great and hoping they don't ask again. Someone who knew you before will usually spot it. When they do, stop and tell them the truth about how the last while has been, and let them respond however they like.

sun.upright:
Endings don't frighten a Scorpio Sun the way they frighten other signs. Your sign's own Major is Death, and you've usually been through a few endings already. You know how to let something go all the way down and come back different. What this card brings that's harder for you is exposure. The Sun lights up everything, and Gemini tells. Whatever ended has ended in the open, other people know the details, and for a sign that keeps its hand very close that can feel like the worst of it.

Gemini and Scorpio are quincunx, five signs apart, with nothing in common and a constant need for small adjustments. Gemini is quick and chatty and doesn't hold on to much. Scorpio's fixed water holds on to everything. So the card's lightness and your depth rub along awkwardly. You might find people treating what happened as last week's news while you're still at the bottom of it. The Sun has no rank in Scorpio and takes its colour from Mars, your traditional ruler, so there's heat in how you take this, anger at whoever you think did it, and with ten swords it can feel like it took several people. That's the betrayal side of this card, and Scorpio feels it keenly.

In the office it's the colleague who took something you told them privately to management. In a relationship it's finding out what you'd half suspected. With a family member it's an old secret out in the open. Decide who gets the real story from you, and keep it to them.
sun.reversed:
A Scorpio Sun can stay down on purpose when this card comes up reversed. You know the thing's over. You've decided you won't forgive it, and there's a kind of power in lying still with the grudge, going over every detail, knowing exactly who said what. Fixed water holds, and Mars colours the Sun in your sign, so the replay has an edge to it.

The Sun also rules the middle ten degrees of Scorpio, the Six of Cups, the card of memory and old times, and upside down that can pull you into the past. You go back over the good years to make the ending hurt more. It shows up as keeping old messages and checking an ex's life online. At work it's a feud that's outlived its reason. Pick one thing you've been keeping as evidence, a message thread, a letter, a folder, and delete it.

moon.upright:
Ten blades in one back. For a Scorpio Moon that's close to the exact shape of the thing you fear most. You don't do casual with feelings. You watch people for a long time, and once you let them in you're fiercely loyal and you expect the same back. So when this card lands on your Moon it's often a betrayal of some kind, a confidence broken, an affair, a friend who went quiet at exactly the wrong moment.

What makes the pairing hard is how little the two signs share. Gemini and Scorpio are quincunx, and the elements, air and water, are strangers who've never been introduced. The card's air wants to explain what happened, understand it, talk it through. A Scorpio Moon feels it somewhere much further down and doesn't want to talk at all. So people offer perspective when what you need is silence and a locked door, and you can come across as cold when you're actually holding an enormous amount. The Sun is a visitor in Scorpio, coloured by Mars, and on your Moon that means heat under the stillness. Anger, a lot of it, kept very quiet.

At home it's the long silence with a partner. With a close friend it's quietly deciding they're out of the inner circle. In the body it's sleep that won't come because you're turning something over. Find a physical way to let some of the anger out, swimming, lifting, anything hard, before you decide what to do about anyone.
moon.reversed:
A Scorpio Moon under the reversed Ten tends to replay the betrayal long after the facts have stopped changing. You go over it at night. You rehearse what you'd say. You check whether the person who hurt you is suffering, and you're disappointed when they seem fine. Fixed water keeps a feeling in one place for a long time, and here it's keeping you there too.

It can also go completely underground, with you insisting you feel nothing about it at all. People close to you notice the chill, though. A partner may feel constantly tested. A friend may sense they're on probation. Tell one person you trust the full, unflattering version of how you feel, the vengeful bits included, and hear how it sounds said aloud.

rising.upright:
Scorpio rising gives very little away on a first meeting. People find you intense, watchful, a bit hard to read, and they often leave feeling you worked out a lot about them and they learned almost nothing about you. Mars is your traditional chart ruler, and there's usually something steady and slightly guarded in how you come into a room. This card, drawn for your mask, pulls against all of that, because it shows something ending in full view.

The Sun is neither helped nor hindered in Scorpio, and it takes on Mars's colouring there. The quincunx between Gemini and Scorpio means the card's openness and your privacy don't fit, and there's constant small adjusting going on. You'll feel it as being on show. People know something happened, maybe everyone at work heard, and you're walking in with that knowledge sitting on you. Scorpio rising usually handles it by going very still and very composed, and to strangers the effect can be striking. They meet someone who's obviously come through something hard and isn't talking about it. Some are drawn in. Some keep their distance.

In a new job it's the rumour you know has reached people before you did. In dating it's being asked what happened with your last relationship and deciding how much to say. With acquaintances it's the silence you use to end a conversation. Choose one person in a new setting and tell them a small true thing about what you've been through, before they hear anything else.
rising.reversed:
Scorpio rising with the card reversed can arrive with the armour doubled. You've recovered from the fall, more or less, and decided nobody's getting that close again, so strangers meet a front that's polite and completely shut. It works. People don't pry. They also don't stay, and a few may decide you're hostile when you're just being careful.

At work it looks like trusting nobody with anything and doing it all yourself. With someone new it's testing them before they've had a chance to prove anything. It can also flip, and you tell a near-stranger far too much in one intense conversation and regret it for days. Somewhere between those two is a version that works. Next time you meet someone you like, let them ask three questions before you decide anything about them.

sun.upright:
The plan was going to work. You believed in it, told everyone about it, maybe moved cities for it. A Sagittarius Sun runs on meaning and on the next horizon, and for most of your life optimism has been a fairly reliable strategy. This card is where the optimism ran out of road. The venture, the move, the teacher or cause you'd given yourself to, has come to a flat, total stop, and it wasn't what you thought it was.

Gemini is your opposite sign. The card sits at the far end of your own axis, facing you, which is why it lands so squarely. Sagittarius deals in the big picture and Gemini deals in the details, and what this card often shows a Sagittarius Sun is every small fact you skipped on the way to the big belief. The Sun is only passing through your sign, coloured by Jupiter, which makes it generous and a little over-confident. Fire and air are friendly elements, so none of this is the end of you, and air feeds fire. Once you've actually taken in what happened, and let it be over, your natural hope has something honest to burn on. That tends to take longer than you'd like. Sagittarius prefers to skip the lying-down part.

In your working life it's the venture you talked everyone into. In study or belief it's a teacher or an idea that let you down. With travel it's the trip, or the move abroad, that went wrong. Go back through the details you didn't want to look at at the time, one by one, before you choose the next direction.
sun.reversed:
When this card is reversed, Sagittarius tends to leave town. Literally, sometimes. The ending came and you booked a flight, took up a new philosophy, found a new cause, and told everyone the whole thing was a blessing in disguise. Maybe it was. But the opposition to Gemini keeps pulling you back to the facts, and they haven't gone anywhere.

At work it's the new project launched to cover the collapse of the last one. With friends it's being the life of every party and not taking calls from anyone who knew you before. In belief it's grabbing the next big idea without checking it. Stay put for a while. Give it a month in one place, doing ordinary things, and let yourself find out what the ending actually cost.

moon.upright:
When things get heavy, you move. A Sagittarius Moon copes by keeping the horizon open, getting outside, laughing about it, finding the meaning in it, booking something. It's a good system and most of the time you bounce. This card tends to catch you on the rare occasion when bouncing doesn't happen, when the thing that ended was too big to joke about and there's nowhere to go. That feels unfamiliar and a bit frightening, because low moods aren't where you usually live.

Gemini sits directly opposite Sagittarius. The card comes from the far side of your own axis, and what Gemini carries is the mind's chatter, the small facts and the words. So the hurt tends to arrive as thoughts. You go over what was said, you read things, you lie awake with sentences. Your Moon wants a bigger picture that makes it all make sense, and the card keeps handing you small details. In your sign the Sun takes on Jupiter's colour, so there's generosity in you even here, and air and fire get on well. Your hope is still there. It just isn't in any hurry, which you'll find annoying.

With a partner it's being restless and short, wanting to leave the room. With friends it's cancelling the plans you'd normally be first to make. In the body it's feeling cooped up and needing air. Go somewhere wide, a beach, a hill, a long empty road, and walk until the thoughts get quieter.
moon.reversed:
A Sagittarius Moon can turn cynical under the reversed Ten, which is hard to watch in someone usually so hopeful. You've been let down, you've got up again, and you've decided not to believe in anything too much in case it happens twice. The jokes get darker. The plans get smaller. Jupiter colours the Sun in your sign, and upside down that big generous hope goes quiet.

Or it goes the other way, restless and escaping, always somewhere else. At home it's never being in. With friends it's saying you're fine from three time zones away. Neither version lets you actually feel what happened. Stay home for a weekend with someone who knew you before the fall, and let them see the tired, unfunny version of you.

rising.upright:
Sagittarius rising walks in with a grin and a story. People meet someone friendly, a bit loud, curious about everything and quick to say yes, and the impression is mostly right. Jupiter rules your Ascendant, and you tend to arrive as if something good is about to happen. Drawn for your mask, this card shows you meeting the world just after something bad did, and the grin's harder to find.

With Sagittarius rising, Gemini is on your Descendant, the cusp of the seventh house, the house of the person opposite you. So the sign this card belongs to sits right on your partnership angle, and it's very common for the ending to have come through a partnership. A marriage, a business partner, a close friend who was the other half of a plan. The two signs oppose each other, a pull toward balance, and when a partnership on that axis ends you feel it in how you meet everyone else. The front you put up is your usual one, cheerful and a bit philosophical. Fire and air get on, so the talk comes easily, and you've probably already got a good line about how it was all for the best. Strangers buy it. People who know you well can see you've been flattened.

At work it's turning up to the first day in a new role after the old one fell apart, and being chirpy about it. In dating it's meeting new people while still carrying the ex. On the road it's the trip taken to get away. Try telling someone new the plain version of what happened, without the lesson you took from it.
rising.reversed:
Sagittarius rising can overdo the comeback when this card comes up reversed. The fall happened, you've mostly recovered, and you're meeting everyone with a slightly manic brightness, big plans, a new place, a new crowd. It's convincing for about ten minutes. People who stay longer notice you don't stop moving long enough to be asked a proper question.

It can also run the other way, a Sagittarius Ascendant gone unusually flat and short with people, the humour turned sour. At work that's the sarcastic remark in a meeting. In a new friendship it's joking about the ex before anyone asked. Slow the first meeting down. Ask the other person about themselves, listen to the whole answer, and leave your own story for another day.

sun.upright:
Somebody built something properly, and it came down anyway. That's close to the worst thing a Capricorn Sun can imagine. You put in years, you take on the responsibility nobody else wanted, and you expect the structure to hold because you did it right. This card is a structure that didn't hold. A role, a business, a marriage, a reputation you'd worked hard for has come down completely, and a Capricorn Sun tends to take that very personally, as if the collapse were a verdict on your competence.

Gemini and Capricorn are quincunx, five signs apart, with nothing in common and constant small adjustment between them. Gemini's quick, restless mind doesn't speak your language, and the elements fight as well, air against earth, talk against proof. So the card's version of the ending, the whole story laid out in the light, might strike you as noise. You want to know what the damage is in actual numbers, and fair enough. The Sun is only a visitor in your sign and takes its colour from Saturn, your ruler, so this card can land with Saturn's weight, heavy and sober, the kind of ending you'll be dealing with in paperwork for a while. The Sun rules the last ten degrees of Capricorn too, the Four of Pentacles, the card of gripping what you've got. That's usually the instinct after a fall like this. Tighten up, protect what's left, trust nobody.

At work it could be a redundancy after twenty years, or a promotion that went elsewhere at the last minute. With money it might be an investment that won't come back. In the family it can be losing your place as the one who holds everything together. Write down, plainly, what you still have after the collapse, and keep the list somewhere you'll see it.
sun.reversed:
A Capricorn Sun with this card reversed is often working harder than ever to prove the collapse didn't happen. You were knocked down. You were back at your desk the next morning, and you've been there since, taking on more, sleeping less, determined nobody sees you rattled. Saturn colours the Sun in your sign, and reversed that turns into endurance for its own sake.

It shows up at work as the extra responsibility you took on to fill the hole. With money it's the tight grip of that Four of Pentacles decan, saving hard and spending nothing on yourself. In the family it's being the rock while you're cracking. Take one full day off with no work in it at all, and tell someone you're doing it so you can't quietly go back in.

moon.upright:
You've probably been praised your whole life for coping well. A Capricorn Moon feels safe when it's in charge of itself, and you deal with feelings the way you deal with anything else, by getting on with it. This card describes a situation you couldn't cope your way out of. Something ended, a loss, a failure, a rejection, and underneath the coping you've gone flat.

The Sun takes Saturn's colouring in your sign, and Saturn rules your Moon, so the card's light here is grey and sober, and it doesn't come with much drama. Gemini and Capricorn are quincunx, and earth and air have little patience with each other. The card wants to think and talk the ending through. Your Moon wants to be left alone to handle it. What you'll recognise is a tiredness that doesn't lift with sleep, and a lot of quiet self-judgement, the voice that says you should have seen it coming, should have planned better, should be over it by now. That's Saturn talking, and it's harsher on you than you'd ever be on a friend.

At work it's burying yourself in tasks and staying late. With family it's being the one who handles the move, the paperwork and the phone calls and never gets to be sad. In the body it's stiffness, the jaw, the back, the shoulders. Ask someone to take one practical job off your hands, and let them do it their way.
moon.reversed:
The reversed Ten on a Capricorn Moon often looks like nothing at all, which is the problem. You've recovered from something serious and never once let anyone see it, and the feeling you didn't have is sitting in your body as tiredness and a short temper. The Sun rules the Four of Pentacles decan at the end of Capricorn, and upside down you can hold on to a feeling the way that card holds on to its coins.

At home this shows as coldness a partner doesn't understand. With friends it's never needing anything. At work it's being very, very reliable and quietly miserable. Tell one person, in a plain sentence, that the last stretch has been hard. You don't have to explain it or ask for anything.

rising.upright:
Capricorn rising looks like it has things in hand. People meet you and see someone composed, a bit formal, older than your years, somebody who'd be good in a crisis. Saturn rules your Ascendant, and that reserve is part of how you keep yourself safe with strangers. In the mask position this card says you're keeping up that front while something underneath it has gone completely.

Earth and air are at cross purposes, and on your Ascendant that's a real split between the steady outside and the story running inside, a worst-case one, followed to its last page. Gemini and Capricorn are quincunx, two signs that never quite line up, and you'll feel the constant small effort of keeping them apart. Nobody at work needs to know. You're right about that, mostly. What tends to happen with Capricorn rising is that people who don't know you well see nothing, and people who do see the stiffness, the way you've gone formal even with them, the jokes you aren't making. The Sun is only a guest in Capricorn, taking Saturn's colour, so the card doesn't blaze out of you. It shows in small ways.

At work it's the professional face during a restructure that's cost you your team. At family events it's being asked how the job's going. In a first meeting with someone new it's deciding whether to mention it at all. Tell one colleague you trust the outline of what happened, just the outline, and leave it at that.
rising.reversed:
When the card is reversed, Capricorn rising can look as if it's turned to stone. The fall is behind you, the recovery's going fine, and your front has set so hard that new people find you forbidding. You're polite and correct and nobody can get past it. Saturn does that. Under pressure it builds walls, and afterwards it forgets to take them down.

In a new job it's being the colleague everyone's slightly scared of. In dating it's the first date that feels like an interview. With younger people it's coming across as disapproving when you're only tired. At home it can be a partner who's stopped asking how you are. Smile at someone first, before they've earned it. It sounds too simple, and for a Capricorn Ascendant it changes a lot of first meetings.

sun.upright:
Count the swords. Ten of them is a lot for one person to have done, and I've seen this card come up for Aquarius Suns when a whole group has closed ranks, a committee, a workplace, an online community, and you were the one left outside. Aquarius puts its faith in ideas and in groups, the project that'll change how things are done, the circle of friends that feels like family, the principle you'd stand by even if it cost you. This card is what it looks like when one of those turns on you, or simply ends.

Gemini trines Aquarius, air to air, and the card moves through you easily. Too easily, maybe. The shared element amplifies, and an Aquarius Sun can meet a painful ending by thinking about it very clearly and feeling almost nothing, or nothing you'd admit to. The Sun is in detriment in Aquarius, the sign opposite its home, which means it has to work against the grain here. Your sense of yourself was never mainly about the spotlight. It comes from being part of something, or from being right. When the something ends, and you're no longer sure you were right, the effort of holding yourself together really shows. Fixed air is stubborn too, so you may still be defending the idea long after it's gone.

At work it could be a project or a movement you believed in, wound up. With friends it's a group that's split and not in your favour. Online it's the pile-on. Step back from the argument for a while and spend time with one person who likes you for reasons that have nothing to do with your views.
sun.reversed:
Upside down, this card can make an Aquarius Sun very cool and very rational about something that hurt a great deal. You've written the analysis. You can explain what went wrong with the group, the project, the relationship, clearly and fairly. What you haven't done is feel any of it, and with the Sun in detriment in your sign that's easy to keep up, since it never liked standing in the middle anyway.

It comes out sideways. At work it's cutting people off completely over a disagreement. Online it's arguing with strangers about something close to the thing that hurt. With friends it's disappearing into a new cause. Tell a friend what the ending actually did to you, in feeling words, sad, humiliated, lonely, whatever's true, and resist explaining why.

moon.upright:
Distance is how you cope. An Aquarius Moon feels safest with a bit of room, friends close enough to talk to and far enough to breathe, and when strong feelings come you step back and look at them from a little way off. That works well until something comes along that's too big to step back from. This card is that. A loss, a friendship over, a group you felt at home in that's no longer yours, and the usual distance won't come.

Gemini trines Aquarius and it's the same element, so the card talks your language. It turns up the head, though. You analyse. You understand exactly what happened and why. The card's planet is in detriment in your Moon sign, working against the grain, and on the Moon that shows as a feeling that has to fight its way through the understanding. It does get through eventually, often at a strange hour and often in a rush that surprises you. Fixed air holds a line for a long time. Plenty of Aquarius Moons describe suddenly finding themselves in tears over something small, a song, a friend's kindness, a dog in the park.

With friends it's the group you've drifted from and miss badly. With a partner it's needing a lot of space and feeling lonely in it. With sleep it's lying awake with your thoughts very clear and very loud. Let one friend see the version of you that isn't coping, and don't turn it into a conversation about ideas.
moon.reversed:
An Aquarius Moon with this card reversed can end up living at a slight distance from its own life. You got through the ending by switching the feelings off, and they haven't come back on. Everything's fine. You're functioning, you're even kind. You're also a bit absent, and the people close to you have noticed.

At home it's being in the room and not really there. With friends it's being the calm one in every crisis and never having one of your own. In the body it can show as odd sleep and a restless, detached tiredness. Air doubled on air makes the head very loud. Do something with your body that needs your full attention, climbing, a hard swim, cooking something difficult, and let the thinking go quiet for an hour.

rising.upright:
Aquarius rising tends to come across as friendly and a little unreachable at the same time. People find you interesting, slightly unusual, easy to talk to about ideas and hard to get close to. Saturn is your traditional chart ruler and Uranus the modern one, and between them you meet the world with some cool and some quirk. Drawn in the mask position, this card means strangers are meeting that cool just after something's ended badly for you, and the cool is doing a lot of work.

The Sun is in detriment in Aquarius. It's out of place in your rising sign and has to go against the grain, which means the card's exposure sits awkwardly on you. Aquarius rising doesn't like being the story. The trine from Gemini, air to air, makes it easy to talk about what happened in the abstract, as if it had happened to somebody else. People find that fascinating or unsettling depending on who they are. What they often don't see is how much of your social world has shifted, the group you used to belong to, the friends who've taken sides.

In a new community, a club, a class, a new city, it's arriving on your own after years of arriving with a crowd. At work it's being the person who spoke up and paid for it. With new friends it's being very good company and very private about the last year. Pick one new group and go back a second and a third time, even when the first visit felt odd.
rising.reversed:
Detachment can go too far for Aquarius rising under the reversed Ten. You've recovered from being pushed out of something, and the lesson you've drawn is that you don't need anyone. Strangers meet a person who seems to want no part of whatever's going on, a bit superior, a bit amused, arms folded. That's rarely how you feel. It's how you've decided to look.

At work it's the contrarian who argues every point in a meeting. At a party it's the corner and the one other person who also doesn't want to be there. Online it's the cutting comment you'd never make in person. Say yes to the next group thing, stay for the whole of it, and let yourself enjoy some of it without making a joke of the enjoying.

sun.upright:
Pisces is the sign that knows how to give in. You can let a thing go, let a feeling wash through, lie still and let the tide do its work in a way tougher signs can't manage. So in one sense this card is familiar ground for a Pisces Sun, because surrender is something you understand. What's harder is the kind of ending it describes. It's made of thoughts and facts, sharp-edged, and Pisces generally deals in something softer.

Gemini squares Pisces. Both are mutable, three signs apart, and that's friction that forces something to move. Gemini names and sorts and explains, and your Sun lives by imagination, by feeling its way. So the card may hand you the plain facts about something you'd rather have kept a little blurred. The relationship was what your friends said it was. The creative dream wasn't going to pay the rent. The person you kept rescuing wasn't going to change. The Sun is a guest in Pisces, coloured by Jupiter and, in modern terms, Neptune, which makes it hopeful and a bit boundless, and that's why the edges of this card can come as a shock. I've watched Pisces Suns take this card very hard and later describe it as the point they got their life back.

With a partner it might be the end of a long, loving hope. With creative work it's a dream finally set down. With a friend or relative you've been looking after, it's admitting you can't save them. Let yourself grieve the hope as a real loss, and give it a proper goodbye, a letter you don't send, a walk to the water.
sun.reversed:
A Pisces Sun with the Ten reversed can get stuck being the one who was wronged. It happened, and it was genuinely awful. Somewhere along the way the story of it became part of who you are, the one who gave everything and got ten swords for it. Pisces' capacity for sacrifice turns inward here, and it can be strangely comforting to stay down.

It shows up in relationships as picking someone who needs rescuing, again. At work it's being taken advantage of and not saying so. With friends it's the same sad story, told a little more beautifully each time. In the evenings it's disappearing into screens, sleep and daydreams. Ask yourself honestly what you'd have to give up if you stopped being the injured party, and then give some of it up.

moon.upright:
Other people's moods, the news, the atmosphere in a room, the sadness of a stranger on the train. A Pisces Moon takes all of it in, and you need regular time on your own, near water or music or sleep, to let it drain back out. This card is a card of too much. One sword would already hurt you, and here there are ten. So what it often shows is overwhelm, a pile-up of hard things, some of them yours and some absorbed from people you love.

Gemini and Pisces are square, both mutable, and the friction is between the quick, sharp mind and the wide, soft heart. The card's swords are words and facts, and for a Pisces Moon words can land like actual blows. A harsh message, a cold remark at work, bad news about someone you love, and you're flattened for days. Air and water are neutral to each other, so it can take a while for what you understand and what you feel to catch up. In Pisces the Sun has no special standing and takes on Jupiter's colour, and Neptune's in the modern scheme, which gives you a wide, forgiving heart. It also makes it hard to tell where your hurt stops and somebody else's starts.

In sleep it's either sleeping far too much or lying awake soaking up everything. With a partner it's needing quiet and not knowing how to ask for it. With friends it's carrying their troubles on top of your own. Spend an hour near water, any water, a bath counts, and don't let anyone reach you while you're there.
moon.reversed:
With the card reversed, a Pisces Moon tends to float off. The worst is behind you and you haven't quite come back into your life. You're sleeping a lot, daydreaming a lot, not answering messages, living in music or films or a long book series, and it feels like rest when half of it is really hiding.

The other form is taking on everyone else's recovery before your own. At home that's looking after a partner who's fine. With friends it's the late-night phone calls you haven't got the energy for. In the body it shows as tiredness with no clear cause. Pick one small, solid thing to do at the same time every day for a couple of weeks, a walk, a meal, a shower before nine, and let it hold you in place.

rising.upright:
People often can't quite pin down Pisces rising. You meet them softly, you pick up their mood and reflect it back, and they leave thinking you were exactly the person they needed to meet. Jupiter rules your Ascendant, Neptune in the modern scheme, and that's where the gentleness and the shape-shifting come from. With this card drawn for your mask, the soft front has had something sharp go through it, and it shows. Strangers tend to see someone tender and a bit worn out.

Gemini is square Pisces, two mutable signs, and there's friction in how the card sits on you. Gemini wants things explained and clearly labelled. Pisces rising prefers to be felt out. So you might find yourself in conversations where people want the facts, what happened, when, whose fault it was, and you can't give them in that form. You just look sad, or you drift off the subject. Air and water have to be introduced before they can work together, and on the Ascendant that shows as a gap between how open you look and how little you're actually saying. Some people are very kind to you. Some take advantage of how soft you seem, and it's worth being alert to that.

At work it's the colleague who offloads onto you because you look like you'll listen. With someone new it's being cast as the fragile one. In crowded shops or on busy trains it's needing to leave early. Before you go into a new room, decide one thing you won't be talked into, and hold to it.
rising.reversed:
Vanishing in plain sight is the risk for Pisces rising when the card's reversed. You turn up, you smile, you agree, and nobody could say afterwards what you thought about anything. After a hard fall, going vague feels safer. It also means people can't find you to help. Neptune has a lot to do with that softness, and so does the square from Gemini, which keeps asking for clear edges you'd rather not draw.

In a new workplace it's letting others decide your role for you. With new friends it's becoming whatever each of them wants. With a new partner it's losing the outline of your own life in theirs very fast. Pick one thing about yourself, an opinion, a taste, a plan, and say it clearly the next time you meet someone, even if it's small and a bit awkward.

1.upright:
The first house is you in the most literal sense, the body, the way you carry yourself, the face you walk into a room with and the way you start things. It's angular, one of the chart's four corners, so whatever lands here is visible. With the Ten of Swords in it, the thing that's ended is a version of you. An old way of presenting yourself, a look, a role you've played so long it passed for your personality, has come to its end.

The astrology here is kinder than the picture. Aries is the first house's natural sign, and the Sun is exalted in Aries, so the card's planet is welcome in this house and does well. Mercury, Gemini's ruler, has its joy here too, and Gemini is sextile Aries, air feeding fire. It adds up to an ending that clears the way for a new start fairly quickly, once you let it be an ending.
