What it feels like from the inside is odder. You may catch yourself in a shop window and not quite recognise the person. Old clothes feel like costumes. The way you used to introduce yourself, the job title, the married name, the one who always organises everything, doesn't fit any more.

In the body it's a tiredness that wants rest and a bit of care. In how you begin things it's hesitating at the start where you'd normally charge in. In your appearance it's wanting a change, a haircut, different clothes, a different way of walking into work. Start with the smallest of those, and let the bigger ones follow later if they still appeal.
1.reversed:
Someone who's got back up but still walks as if another blow's coming. That's the usual look of the reversed Ten in the first house. The shoulders stay up. You flinch at small criticisms. Starting anything new feels risky, because the last thing you started ended flat on the ground. This is an angular house and a visible one, so people notice the wariness before they notice you.

It shows up in the body as tension and a guarded posture, and in how you begin things, with a lot of preparation and not much launch. In your looks it can be dressing to disappear. Mars rules this house naturally and Mars wants action. Take one small, physical step forward, a new class, a different route to work, and let your body find out it's allowed to move again.

2.upright:
Money you can actually count, what you own, what you earn, and the harder question of what you think you're worth. That's the second house, a succedent house, the place where you build things up and hold on to them. Drawn into this house, the card points to a financial ending. It might be a job's income stopping, a business winding up, an investment that won't come back, or the end of a way of spending you can no longer afford.

Air and earth are the two elements least alike, and in the house of Taurus that shows as the gap between the story about the money and the money itself. The card's air is worry and scenarios, run to the worst possible end. The house's earth is the bank balance. Most people who draw this here have been living in the story for a while, lying awake doing sums that come out differently each time. Gemini sits next to Taurus, a semi-sextile, and each has what the other lacks. What Gemini can bring to this house is the willingness to look plainly and name the figures. What the house asks back is patience, because money rebuilds slowly and in physical amounts, one pay packet at a time.

With the actual money it's sitting down with the real numbers, all of them. With self-worth it's noticing how much of your sense of yourself was riding on what you earned or owned. With possessions it can be letting things go, selling the car, clearing out the storage unit. Write the true figures on one page, income, outgoings, debts, and read them in daylight.
2.reversed:
In the money house, the reversed card usually means the financial low has passed and you're still living as if it hasn't. Every purchase feels dangerous. You check the account three times a day, turn down things you can afford, and treat any small bill as a sign the collapse is coming back. Or it's the reverse, spending to feel normal again before the ground's really solid.

Venus is this house's natural ruler, and she's about what you value and what you enjoy, and both tend to shrink when you're braced for another fall. With a partner it shows as arguments about money that are really about fear. With self-worth it's accepting less pay because you're grateful for anything. Set a small, fixed amount each fortnight that's purely for pleasure, and spend all of it.

3.upright:
This card belongs to the third house in a way few cards do. Gemini is the house's own sign, and the Ten of Swords is a Gemini card, so it's on home ground, speaking the local language, and whatever it brings is turned up loud. The third house is everyday talk, emails and texts, the neighbourhood, short trips, brothers and sisters, and the way you learn. What's ended is something in that everyday world of words.

It might be a conversation that finally said the last thing. A long-running argument with a sibling that's reached its final sentence. A course that didn't work out, or a way of thinking about something that's run its full length. The Sun lights up the whole of it, and in the third house that tends to mean you've heard or read or said everything there is. It can feel almost physically tiring, like a head that's been talking for days. The Moon has its joy in this house, and there's a feeling side to all this chatter that's easy to miss. Under the words is usually a hurt that nobody's named.

With a brother or sister it's an old way of relating reaching its end, painful but clear. In the local area it might be leaving a street you've known for years. On your phone it's the thread you finally stop replying to. Write the last thing you'd want to say, to the person or about the thing, and then decide whether to send it at all.
3.reversed:
The third house reversed often shows a mind that can't stop narrating. The ending happened, and your head is still drafting replies, rehearsing arguments, rereading messages for what they really meant. The card and the house share an element, air on air, so upside down the chatter doubles. Sleep suffers. So does concentration, and you might find you've read the same page four times.

With a sibling it can be an old row that keeps getting reopened in the family chat. In study it's giving up on something because one bad result felt final. On short trips you know by heart it's being distracted and a bit careless. Set a limit on how often you'll talk about it, to anyone, and when you reach it, talk about something else.

4.upright:
A family home sold. A household broken up by a move or a divorce. An old family story finally told in full, so nobody can pretend any more. The fourth house is home, the actual house or flat, the family you come from, and the private ground under your life that most people never see. It's angular, one of the chart's corners, so what happens here isn't small even when it's quiet. With the Ten of Swords in it, something at home has ended.

Gemini sits just before Cancer, the sign that naturally belongs to this house, a semi-sextile. Neighbours, with not much in common. Air and water are neutral to one another and need introducing. So the card's way of handling an ending, talking it through, laying it all out, doesn't fit easily into the house of the Moon, where endings are felt in the gut and carried in memory. You might find the family has explained the whole thing to each other in detail and nobody feels any better. Or you're packing boxes, perfectly organised, and you find a drawing a child did years ago and have to sit down on the floor.

With parents it might be a change in who looks after whom, or a painful conversation about the past. With the house itself it's leaving or clearing a place. In your private life it's the rooms that feel different with someone gone. Take one object from the old home and give it a clear place in whatever comes next.
4.reversed:
With the Ten reversed in the fourth house, the family trouble is over and the house hasn't got its warmth back. Everyone's being careful. The rooms are tidy and a bit silent. Sometimes one person is still refusing to let it end, bringing up the sale, the divorce, the old grievance at every gathering, and the whole family bends round them.

Privately it can look like not wanting to go home, working late, finding reasons to be out. With a parent it can be an apology that hasn't been made. The Moon rules this house, and it recovers through small daily care, the kind nobody makes a fuss about. Cook a proper meal, even for two, and eat it together at the table with the phones in another room.

5.upright:
The fifth house is where you play. Romance, creative work, hobbies, children and the time you spend with them, anything you do because it's a pleasure. The Sun is this house's natural ruler and also the card's planet, so the Ten of Swords is on home turf here and speaks with some force. What's ended is something you loved doing, or someone you loved in that early, playful way.

It might be a romance that finished before it got serious and hurt more than you'd expected. It might be a creative project, a band, a book, a small business built out of a hobby, that's come to a hard stop. Leo is the house's sign and Gemini is sextile to it, air feeding fire, which is partly why this ending tends to come with so much story attached. You'll have talked about it, pictured it, imagined how it would go, and the imagining is part of what's been lost. Venus has her joy in this house as well, so there's a real sense of pleasure having drained out of things, as if someone turned the colour down a notch. Food tastes flatter. The music you liked doesn't do much.

In love it's the fling or the new relationship that's over. With children it might be a stage that's finished, the little years gone, or a hard stretch with a teenager. With your creative life it's the project you're putting in a drawer. Do one small playful thing that has no future in it at all, a game, a terrible drawing, singing along in the car.
5.reversed:
Upside down in the fifth house, the Ten often means you've stopped playing. The romance ended, the creative thing folded, and since then you haven't let yourself enjoy much, in case it goes the same way. Pleasure feels risky. Dating feels like a job interview. The guitar's in the cupboard.

It can also go the other way, a string of short romances or new hobbies picked up and dropped, none of them allowed to matter. With children it can mean being over-careful with them, or not quite present at their games because your head's elsewhere. In love it's comparing everyone new with what ended. Pick one thing you used to love doing for fun and do it badly, with nobody watching, for an hour.

6.upright:
You've been running on a routine for a long time, overworking, under-sleeping, keeping every plate spinning, and it's come to a stop. The sixth house is the daily grind in the plainest sense, your routine, the job you do day to day, the way you look after your body, the chores, the pets, the small habits that keep everything going. The Ten of Swords here is a routine that's broken down under its own weight.

Gemini squares Virgo, the sign that goes with this house, and air and earth are at odds, so what you'll recognise is a mind that's been doing the work of a body. Lists in your head at three in the morning. Worry standing in for rest. Mercury rules this house and also rules Gemini, and the two Mercury signs grind at right angles. Mars has its joy here, which is why the sixth can take a lot of effort and keep going, until the day it can't, and this card is that day. What it asks for is rest and support, the unglamorous kind, and it isn't saying anything worse than that about your body.

At work it's a job that's burned you out, or a role that's been cut. In the body it's tiredness that needs sleep, proper food and probably the check-up you've been putting off. With daily routines it's the gym habit, the meal prep, the early starts, some of which may need to go. Take one thing off your daily list entirely, and put a regular bedtime in its place.
6.reversed:
Reversed in the sixth house, the card tends to show someone back at work too early. You've had the collapse, the burnout, the bad patch, and you're already doing everything again at full speed because stopping felt so frightening. Mars loves this house, and Mars doesn't like resting. Upside down it can push the body past what it's got.

It also shows as routines kept up out of fear, rigid meal plans, strict training, a to-do list that runs your life. At work it can look like never taking leave. With pets or the people you care for day to day, it's doing everything yourself. Build one day into each week where you plan to do very little, and treat it as fixed.

7.upright:
The seventh house is the person opposite you. A partner, a husband or wife, a business partner, anyone you've signed something with, and also the open enemy, the person you're in a formal dispute with. It's angular, one of the corners, so what happens here is visible and it matters. The Ten of Swords in the seventh is a partnership reaching its absolute end, a marriage, a business arrangement, a long collaboration.

There's real friction in the astrology. Libra is this house's natural sign, and the Sun is in fall in Libra, uncomfortable and unheard. The Sun wants to stand in the middle and shine as itself. The seventh house wants two people meeting halfway. So a Sun card in the partnership house often describes a relationship in which one person, maybe you, maybe them, needed more room to be themselves than the arrangement could give. Gemini trines Libra, air to air, so there's been plenty of talking about it, probably for years, and the talk amplifies. By now both of you can recite each other's side. What's left is the ending itself.

With a spouse or long-term partner it's separation, or the end of a particular way of being together. In business it's dissolving a partnership, contracts closed, accounts split. In a dispute it's the point where both sides stop arguing because there's nothing left to argue about. If there's paperwork, get it done cleanly and fairly, and keep your conversations with them short and practical while you do.
7.reversed:
A partnership has ended and one of you won't let it. It might be you, still ringing, still checking in, still negotiating over things that were settled long ago. It might be them. Either way the ending keeps getting reopened, and every conversation starts the old argument again in a new place. That's the reversed Ten in the seventh house, and it's tiring for everyone.

In business it's a partnership formally closed with loose ends that keep flaring up, an unpaid invoice, a shared client. With an ex it's the friendship you're trying to keep that keeps hurting. With a new partner it can be keeping one foot back because of what happened last time. Agree one clear boundary with the person from before, write it down if that helps, and hold to it.

8.upright:
Shared money, debts, inheritances, a partner's finances, sex and the trust it needs, and endings of the deep kind, the ones that change you. The eighth house covers what people don't usually talk about at dinner. It's succedent, a house where things build up and are held, sometimes for years. What this card brings to it is a deep ending. Something shared has come apart, or a trust has been broken so thoroughly there's no going back to how it was.

Gemini and Scorpio, the eighth's natural sign, are quincunx, with nothing in common and constant adjusting needed. Air and water are strangers to each other. The card talks and explains. The eighth house feels and keeps quiet. So you might be getting a lot of explanation, from a partner, from an adviser, from yourself, about something no explanation really touches. The house is ruled by Mars, and in modern astrology by Pluto, and that's where the intensity comes from. Nothing ends lightly here, and all ten swords fit how it feels. The eighth is also the house of what comes after an ending, and that part isn't in the picture yet.

With shared money it might be separating finances, closing a joint account, sorting out a debt someone left you with. In intimacy it's the end of a sexual relationship, or of the trust in one, and the loneliness after. With family it can be an estate, a will, the practical side of a loss. Get the money side properly finished, with help if you need it, so what's left to deal with is only the feeling.
8.reversed:
A deep ending that's still being held on to is what the reversed Ten usually shows in the eighth. The joint account's closed and you still check theirs. The affair's over and you go back over the messages. A debt's been paid and you still feel owned by it. Fixed water keeps things, and upside down this card keeps the wound open to look at.

Mars, the traditional ruler here, wants to act, and a lot of that energy goes into going over what's finished. In intimacy it can show as holding back with someone new, or testing them hard to see if they'll betray you too. With shared money it's being secretive, or suspicious of a partner's spending. Pick one practical thread that ties you to the old situation, a password, a direct debit, a box of letters, and cut it.

9.upright:
The Sun has its joy in the ninth house, the one house it traditionally loves most, so the card's planet does its best work here. That makes the Ten of Swords in the ninth an unusual one. The ninth is where you go looking for meaning, beliefs, study, religion or philosophy, travel to far places, teachers, publishing, the big questions. The ending this card brings is bright and total, and it's about something you believed.

Gemini sits opposite Sagittarius, the ninth's own sign, and the card pulls from the far end of that axis. Gemini is facts and local detail. The ninth is meaning and the long view. So what often happens is that one detail brings down a whole belief. One conversation, one piece of news, one thing you learned about a teacher or a community or a cause, and the whole structure of meaning goes. Fire and air get along, and the Sun is happy in this house, so there's often clarity in it, even relief. You can see exactly why you believed what you believed and why you can't any more.

In study it could be a degree or a course that finished badly, or a subject you've outgrown. With faith or philosophy it's the end of a belief you held for years. With travel it's a plan to live abroad falling through, or coming home from somewhere for good. What do you still believe, once this has gone? Write it down in a few lines, even if the list is much shorter than it used to be.
9.reversed:
A belief has collapsed and you're refusing to replace it. That's often the reversed card in the ninth house. You've been burned by a teacher, a church, a movement, a big idea, and you've decided you won't believe in anything that big again. It's understandable. It can also leave life feeling small and a bit grey, which in the house where the Sun has its joy is a real loss.

The other form is rushing to the next belief, the next guru, the next course, before you've worked out what went wrong with the last. In travel it can be restlessness with nowhere to go. In study it's starting something and dropping it. Read one thing, slowly, by someone who disagrees with what you used to believe, and see what you still agree with.

10.upright:
The tenth house is the top of the chart, your public role and reputation, the job title, what people who barely know you would say you do. It's angular and very visible. With the Ten of Swords here, a career chapter has ended, and it's ended in public. A role made redundant, a business that closed, a demotion or a sacking, a reputation hit hard by something everyone in your field seems to have heard about.

Capricorn is the house's natural sign and Saturn its ruler, and Gemini is quincunx Capricorn, five signs apart, with nothing to say to each other. The elements pull apart too, air against earth, talk against proof. That's exactly how a public career ending tends to feel. There's a lot of talk, the rumours, the explanations, the version your old employer is telling, and none of it changes the facts on the ground, which are that the job's gone. Saturn's house is slow and serious, and it rebuilds slowly and seriously. It usually rewards people who can tell the truth about what happened and get back to work, in time. This card has the Sun in it, which lights everything, so keeping it quiet isn't really on offer.

At work it's the role that's gone, and the professional contacts you have to face. With your reputation it's deciding what you'll say when people ask. With your parents, if they're part of how you measure success, it's telling them. Write the two-sentence version of what happened, true and plain, and use it every time.
10.reversed:
In the career house the reversed card often shows someone still wearing a job that's gone. The title's still in your email signature. You introduce yourself by the old role. You apply for identical positions because anything else feels like admitting a fall. Saturn rules this house and Saturn is patient, but upside down it can turn patience into refusing to move.

The other version is avoiding the public side of work altogether, turning down anything visible, keeping your head low because the last time you stood up you got knocked flat. With colleagues from before it's being defensive. In interviews it's explaining the gap at length before anyone's asked. Update one public thing, a profile, a bio, a business card, so it describes where you actually are.

11.upright:
The Sun doesn't sit well in this house's sign, and that sets the tone. The eleventh is your friends, the groups you belong to, your networks, and your hopes, the things you'd like your life to include in five years. It's succedent, where connections build and hold. With this card in the eleventh, something in that circle has ended. A friendship group broken up. A team, a club, a community you felt part of, gone or turned against you. Or a hope you'd carried for years, finally shown to be something that won't happen.

Aquarius is the eleventh's natural sign, and the Sun is in detriment there, working against the grain. The card's way of doing things, full exposure and one figure in the spotlight, doesn't suit what the eleventh wants, which is the group, everyone together. So this ending often has an isolating quality, with one person ending up outside the circle. Gemini trines Aquarius, air to air, and there's usually a lot of talk around it, the group chat, the messages, people passing on who said what, all of it amplified. Jupiter has its joy in this house, though, and in many charts I've seen friendship grow back here, generously and sometimes from unexpected directions.

With friends it's losing a group, or the one friend who was the centre of it. In networks or a professional body it's a falling-out. With your hopes it's a wish for the future you've had to set down. Leave the group chat, or mute it, and make a plan with one person who stuck by you.
11.reversed:
With the Ten reversed in the eleventh, the falling-out's done and you're still following it from the outside. You keep up with what the old group's doing. You hear who said what about you. You avoid places they might be. It keeps the ending alive in a way that stops you finding new people, and fixed air, the sign of this house, can hold a grudge in the head for years.

With hopes it's refusing to hope for anything new in case it goes the same way. In networks it's avoiding events in your field. With the friends who did stay, it's taking them a bit for granted. Ring one of those friends, thank them properly, and suggest something you'd both enjoy.

12.upright:
The twelfth house is what goes on out of sight. Sleep and dreams, time alone, the things you do in private and the things you don't let yourself know about yourself. It's cadent, a house where things get processed and let go. The Ten of Swords here is an ending nobody else can see. Something has finished inside you, a hope, a fear, a long private story about yourself, and it's reached its last line.

Gemini squares Pisces, the sign that goes with this house, two mutable signs grinding. The card's mind wants to explain and the twelfth house doesn't do explanations. The card's air and the house's water neither clash nor help each other, and here they meet in sleep. You might be dreaming vividly, or waking at four with the whole thing going round. The Sun lights everything in this card, and in the twelfth that can mean something you'd kept buried coming up in the quiet hours, an old grief, a regret, something you did years ago and never spoke about. Saturn has its joy in the twelfth, and that suits this card, since Saturn is at ease with solitude and with things being finished privately and properly.

In sleep it's the dreams and the early waking. With time alone it's needing more of it, and making real room for it. In your private habits it's something you've been keeping from yourself that's finally out. Go somewhere quiet on your own for half a day, a church, a beach, a library, and let whatever's finished be finished there.
12.reversed:
A private ending kept private too long is what the reversed Ten tends to show in the twelfth. You've come through something hard and told no one. The recovery is happening in secret, and so is the replaying, in the shower, on long drives, in the middle of the night. The twelfth hides things well, and upside down it hides them from the people who could help.

It can also show as escaping into sleep, screens or daydreams. With the people close to you it's being there in body and absent everywhere else. Jupiter, and Neptune in the modern scheme, rule this house, and both can make it very easy to drift. Tell one person, even a professional, the thing you've been carrying alone, and let it stop being a secret.
